Chapter 10. The Ongoing Invitation: Living the Mystery.
At the heart of it all, the teachings of Christ aren’t really about following a strict set of rules.
Instead, they’re an invitation—an open door to a way of living that’s humble, present, and ready to embrace the mystery at the center of everything.
Imagine a group of friends, sitting around a table, swapping stories about their lives. They talk about faith and doubt, moments of pure joy, and times of real sorrow. There are days when Christ’s presence feels so close, almost tangible. And other days? Well, He seems distant, and the questions just keep coming.
Listening to each other, it’s clear: the journey never really ends, does it? There’s always something new to discover, another lesson to learn, more to receive.
In the East, people often describe the spiritual path as a journey with no finish line—just a continuing unfolding, a deepening into mystery. When you look at Christ’s teachings this way, the invitation becomes ongoing. There’s no final arrival, no moment when all your questions are answered. There’s just the next step, the next breath, and the next chance to love.
Most of us want closure. We crave that sense of being done, of having everything wrapped up neatly. But the real invitation? It’s to live with open hands. To welcome the unknown. To trust that the journey itself—right here, right now—is the destination.
Think of a child learning to ride a bike. They fall, probably more than once. But there’s always someone there—a parent, a friend—ready to help them up, to cheer them on, to remind them that falling is part of learning.
Little by little, the child gets more confident. They start to risk more, and pretty soon, they’re laughing, enjoying the ride. It’s not about being perfect. It’s about learning, growing, and sharing the journey together.
Here’s something to pay attention to: the mystery of Christ isn’t a puzzle to solve. It’s something to live into.
It’s found in the willingness to show up, to be present, and to love—with no strings attached.
It’s the invitation to step into the unknown, and to trust that, even when we’re confused or full of doubt, there’s a presence holding everything—yes, even us—together.
